column3: NKJV has “very great” and names “Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “again there was a great crowd … He called.”
Close to the Greek; “desolate place” is rendered “wilderness.”
Close to the Greek; “baskets” is rendered “large baskets.”
NKJV renders the Hebrew-style oath “if a sign will be given” as the plain negative “no sign shall be given.”
NKJV has “saying, ‘It is because we have no bread,’” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “that they had no bread.”
NKJV names “Jesus” and includes “still,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Do you have your heart hardened?”
Close to the Greek; NKJV supplies “I broke.”
NKJV has “How is it you do not understand?,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Do you not yet understand?”
NKJV has “made him look up,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “he looked intently.”
NKJV includes “nor tell anyone in the town,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “Do not even enter the village.”
